newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA ROUT INDIA TO WIN ASIA CUP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA ROUT INDIA TO WIN ASIA CUP.

text.p: World champions Sri Lanka, spurred by impressive innings from their openers and skipper, routed India by eight wickets to win the Asia Cup at home on Saturday.
They won in style, batting second and knocking the 240 runs needed for victory with 13 overs to spare.
"Sri Lanka played like world champs and we didn't have a chance," said Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar.
"Their fielding was excellent with about two or three superb catches. We fell short by about 20 or 30 runs," he added.
Sanath Jayasuriya set the pace for Sri Lanka with a blistering knock of 63 off 52 balls (two sixes, eight fours) sharing a first wicket stand of 137 off 109 balls with Mavan Atapattu.

After the quick exit of Aravinda de Silva, who made six before holing a return catch to Saurav Ganguly, skipper Arjuna Ranatunga and Atapattu shared an unbroken third wicket stand of 96 runs off 104 balls to seal Sri Lanka's victory.
Atapattu finished with an undefeated 84 scored off 101 balls with one six and six fours to take the Man of the Match award, his second in the competition

Ranatunga was unbeaten on 62 scored off 67 deliveries with three sixes and five fours. The innings carried his series tally to 272 runs from four matches at an average of 136.00 and gave him the Man of the Series award.
"Everything worked out according to our plan and we managed to restrict India to a total of around 240 on a good batting wicket due to some excellent fielding and bowling," Ranatunga said.
The victory ended India's run as Asia Cup champions since 1988. They had defended the title successfully in India and in Sharjah.
It was Sri Lanka's second Asia Cup win following their first in 1986 when they last hosted it.
Earlier former captain Mohammad Azharuddin scored 81 to steer India to a total of 239 for seven wickets after Tendulkar had won the toss and decided to bat first.
Azharuddin who scored an undefeated 81 in the league match against Sri Lanka, made an identical score off 102 balls with two sixes and one four.
With Tendulkar, Azharuddin shared a fourth wicket partnership of 109 off 140 balls to help India achieve the total.
Tendulkar hit two fours in his 67 balls innings, as he and Azharuddin rescued India from a shaky position of 59 for 3 in 18 overs.
India's total would have been much higher had it not been for some excellent fielding and catching by the Sri Lankans.

Roshan Mahanama, one of the finest fielders in the side brought off a superb one-handed catch at mid wicket to send back Rahul Dravid for seven, and there were three other catches that went quite close to matching it.
